slides.label: Contracts
slides.headline: Signed a freehold pre-con deal? There's *no 10-day cooling-off*.

slides.label: Condo vs freehold
slides.headline: Condos get 10 days. *Freehold doesn't.*
slides.body: The 10-day right comes from the Condominium Act. A freehold detached or townhome agreement is firm once you sign.

slides.label: The exception
slides.headline: *POTL* townhomes.
slides.body: A parcel of tied land belongs to a common elements condo, so a 10-day right may apply. Check the agreement.

slides.label: What to do
slides.headline: The review happens *before* you sign.
slides.body: Have a lawyer read it first, or ask the builder for a lawyer-review condition.

caption:
The most expensive misunderstanding in pre-con: assuming you get 10 days to back out.

That right is for condos. On a freehold detached or townhome, the deal is firm the moment you sign.
